clue.text: Still a profit, and not for the first time

parts.note: still, as in 'there is yet time', means yet
a profit is a gain

explanation.surface: A trader notes that the business has made money once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something again means repeating it, so it is not happening for the first time.

clue.text: Cowardly way to react loudly to pain

parts.note: to react loudly is to yell
ow is the cry one makes in pain

explanation.surface: Shouting in pain is called a coward's response.
explanation.definitionFit: Being yellow is slang for lacking courage, being a coward.

clue.text: Not a silent lecture that is

parts.note: a lecture is a talk
ie is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A spoken lecture, that is, rather than a quiet one.
explanation.definitionFit: An early sound film with spoken dialogue was so called to distinguish it from a silent film.

clue.text: Gran is disposed to suggest cereals

indicators.note: disposed in the sense of arranged tells us the letters of Gran is are set out differently

explanation.surface: Grandma is inclined to recommend breakfast foods.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereals such as wheat and barley are grains.

clue.text: Hindu social centre needs gym equipment

parts.note: a Hindu is typically Indian
a club is a centre for social gatherings

explanation.surface: A Hindu community hall requires some exercise apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: These bottle-shaped wooden weights are swung in exercise routines in a gymnasium.

clue.text: Never again exhausted

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'not any longer, ever' and also describes a supply that has run out completely.

clue.text: Where a bull and magpie appear to schedule

definitions.text: Where a bull and magpie appear

explanation.walkthrough: On a shooting target the bull is the centre and the magpie the ring just outside it, so both are found on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullseye and magpie are rings on a shooter's board, and the phrase also means progressing as planned.

clue.text: John to be redeployed at work

indicators.note: redeployed suggests the letters of John to be are moved into new positions

explanation.surface: John is due to be moved to a different post.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone working in a role is busy, doing it right now.

clue.text: Calm down when put in peril

explanation.walkthrough: Split as END ANGER the letters ask you to stop being cross, while the whole word means to threaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Read in two parts it is an instruction to cease rage; as one word it means to expose to danger.

clue.text: Wycliffites all turned into peers

indicators.note: into tells us one piece goes inside the other, here inside the peers

parts.note: peers of the realm are lords

indicators.note: turned asks for the word all to be read backwards

explanation.surface: Followers of John Wycliffe were all ennobled.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lollards followed John Wycliffe, the 14th-century English reformer who translated the Bible; 'peers' in the surface reads as equals but means members of the nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lollards were the religious movement that followed the teachings of John Wycliffe.

clue.text: Condition applied to the date laid down

indicators.note: applied to means one piece is attached on to the other, so the letter follows

parts.note: a condition, as in a state of health, is a state

explanation.surface: Some condition has been attached to the appointed day.
explanation.definitionFit: Rules that are laid down are set out or declared, which is what stated means.

clue.text: Relation settled in the East

indicators.note: settled suggests the letters of relation have been resettled into a new order

explanation.surface: A family member has gone to live in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is the East, so the adjective describes things found or originating there.

clue.text: One German pursues killer whale to obtain dye

indicators.note: pursues means the German piece comes after the whale, chasing it

parts.note: an orc is an old name for the killer whale or orca
ein is German for one

explanation.surface: A German hunts an orca in order to get a colouring agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Orcein is a red-purple colouring obtained from lichens and used as a stain in microscopy.

clue.text: Polish physicist and French husband get key to remedy including iodine

parts.note: mari is French for husband
E is a musical key

indicators.note: including means one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: a remedy is a cure
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A Polish scientist and her French spouse find the key to a cure that contains iodine.
explanation.walkthrough: Marie Curie, born in Warsaw, won Nobel prizes in physics and chemistry with her French husband Pierre.
explanation.definitionFit: The pioneer of radioactivity research was a Polish-born physicist working in France.

clue.text: Just get there and prepare the house for repainting

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to arrive or win by a narrow margin, and taken literally it means stripping old paint from a dwelling.

clue.text: Everywhere everyone is obese

parts.note: everyone means all
an obese person can be described as round

explanation.surface: All over the place, everybody is overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something found on every side, in all directions, is everywhere.

clue.text: It sounds like farewell to a bargain

indicators.note: it sounds like tells us the answer is pronounced like a phrase for parting

parts.note: a farewell is a goodbye

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye to something cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well worth the price is a bargain purchase.

clue.text: Bully time for cheap passenger accommodation

parts.note: a bully here is a young bull or bullock, which is a steer
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A thug spends ages in the cheapest seats on board.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest-priced section of an old passenger ship, near the rudder gear, was the steerage.

clue.text: Anything but heavy rock!

parts.note: heavy rock is loud music, and its opposite is a gentle, easy-listening style; the exclamation flags the play on heavy versus not heavy

explanation.definitionFit: Easy, melodic orchestral pieces are the genre lying opposite heavy metal on the musical scale.

clue.text: Kind chap put in the shade De

indicators.note: put in means the chap is placed inside the shade

parts.note: a shade of colour is a hue
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A kind man is left in the shadows.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane means compassionate and considerate towards others.

clue.text: I am upset by doctor with sex appeal making a bloomer

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces sit side by side
upset in a down clue means the contraction of I am is turned upside down

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: I'm distressed by a seductive doctor making a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IM into MI. 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimosa is a flowering shrub, and a bloomer is something that flowers.

clue.text: Small amount of pudding

explanation.definitionFit: A little bit is a trifle, and so is the layered dessert of sponge, custard and cream.

clue.text: Rumour voiced by bed-sit resident

indicators.note: voiced means we want a word that sounds like rumour when spoken

parts.note: taken as the word spoken

explanation.surface: Gossip is spread by someone living in a rented room.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodger who rents a single room, as in a bedsit, is a mainly American term for a lodger.

clue.text: Happen to consume a pastry dish meant for the man of the house

indicators.note: to consume means one piece swallows the other, holding it inside

parts.note: to happen is to occur
a pie is a dish baked in pastry

explanation.surface: A man of the house happens to eat a pie meant for him.
explanation.definitionFit: The person living in a home, its resident or householder, is its occupier.

clue.text: Cheerful despite being the last in the players' bar

definitions.text: the last in the players' bar

explanation.walkthrough: The players are musicians: the final, unaccented beat of a bar, leading into the next downbeat, has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means optimistic in mood, and in music it names the weak beat that ends a measure.

clue.text: Suddenly stop to get a piece from a slab of chocolate

definitions.text: to get a piece from a slab of chocolate

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to halt abruptly, and literally to snap a square away from a chocolate bar.

clue.text: Does his poetry make for uninteresting study?

definitions.text: Does his poetry make for uninteresting study?

parts.note: dull, uninteresting prose is dry
a den is a private room for study

explanation.surface: Is this poet's verse a dull read?
explanation.walkthrough: John Dryden was a 17th-century English poet; the whole clue both defines him and gives the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was the leading English poet of the Restoration era, so his poetry is the subject asked about.

clue.text: Tea never served but to show deep respect

indicators.note: served suggests the letters of tea never are dished up in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Tea is never handed round except as a mark of honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere someone is to honour them with deep respect.
